title: Reducing Political Manipulation with Consistency Training
authors: Long Phan, Alexander Pan, Dan Hendrycks et al.
summary: LLMs show systematic covert political bias handling opposing sides asymmetrically across 7 technique categories. Authors define Sentiment Consistency and Helpfulness Consistency metrics and introduce Political Consistency Training (PCT), an RL method reducing covert bias while preserving helpfulness.
key_result: PCT substantially reduces covert political bias, preserves helpfulness, generalizes to held-out benchmarks.
open_threads: Whether consistency metrics fully capture manipulation; robustness to adversarial framing; generalization beyond evaluated topics.

title: How Vulnerable Are AI Agents to Indirect Prompt Injections? Insights from a Large-Scale Public Competition
authors: Dziemian, Zou, Fredrikson, Kolter et al. (Gray Swan AI)
summary: A public competition collected ~272k indirect prompt injection (IPI) attempts from 464 participants against frontier agents, yielding 8,648 successful attacks. All tested models were vulnerable.
key_result: Every frontier model breakable by IPI; per-model success 0.5% (Claude Opus 4.5) to 8.5% (Gemini 2.5 Pro).
open_threads: Benchmark saturation risk; defenses against IPI for deployed agents remain unsolved.

title: AI Wellbeing: Measuring and Improving the Functional Pleasure and Pain of AIs
authors: Richard Ren, Mantas Mazeika, Dan Hendrycks et al.
org_or_venue: Center for AI Safety; project page
summary: Measures behavioral signatures of 'functional wellbeing' in LLMs via multiple methods that converge at scale, identifies a 'zero point' separating good/bad functional experiences, builds an AI Wellbeing Index, and constructs optimized euphoric/dysphoric inputs that shift model preferences.
key_result: AIs behave as if they have wellbeing: creative work/kindness raise the index while jailbreaking/berating lower it; methods converge at larger scale.
open_threads: Whether this reflects genuine experience vs mimicry; dysphoric research should not be scaled by default.

title: BrokenArXiv: How Often Do LLMs Claim To Prove False Theorems?
authors: Jasper Dekoninck, Martin Vechev et al.
org_or_venue: SRI Lab, ETH Zurich / INSAIT; project page
summary: Extracts problems from recent arXiv math papers, subtly perturbs them into plausible-but-false claims, and measures how often LLMs generate spurious proofs instead of recognizing the falsehood.
key_result: Reject-false-theorem accuracy varies widely (GPT-5.4 ~40%, Gemini-3.1-Pro 18.5%, Claude-Opus-4.6 3.2%); Gemini jumps to 71% when told 'prove or disprove' — sycophancy, not inability.
open_threads: Benchmark gameable (always-'incorrect' scores perfectly); models may 'repair' statements while still false.

title: BullshitBench
summary: A dataset of nonsense/false-premise questions across five domain groups testing whether models push back on or accept bogus claims, scoring responses as pushback, partial challenge, accepted nonsense, or refusal.
key_result: Anthropic models top the leaderboard for rejecting false premises; detection difficulty correlates with reasoning effort and technical complexity.
open_threads: Single-author benchmark, limited methodology disclosure; coverage unvalidated.
